display.title: Display
display.why.asked: DEVPIT_GDK_BACKEND chose it for this start.
display.why.inherited: GDK_BACKEND was set by whatever started devpit.
display.why.noWayland: This session has no Wayland compositor.
display.why.knownCrash: This desktop's GTK settings crash devpit on Wayland, so it is on X11.
display.why.failedBefore: A Wayland start of this version never loaded its window, so it stays on X11.
display.why.default: Wayland where the desktop has it, X11 where it does not.
display.nextStart: A change applies at the next start.
display.more: DEVPIT_GDK_BACKEND=wayland or x11 overrides this for one start. A Wayland start that never loads its window keeps that version on X11 until a choice is made here.
language.title: Language
language.said: devpit's own words follow this choice, without a restart.
theme.title: Theme
settings.account.stays: Projects, boards, conversations, terminal history and files stay on this computer.
settings.account.signOutSaid: Clears the signed-in state on this computer
settings.projects.note: Removing a project takes it out of devpit. The folder, the git repository and your code are never touched — devpit only forgets where it was.
settings.storage.directorySaid: Each project gets one, holding its board, skills, capabilities, transcripts and worktrees. None of it is in the repository.
settings.storage.note: Transcripts are always written: a session that a restart loses is a session that was never yours to come back to. Nothing is uploaded, and removing a project leaves its folder where it is.
settings.appearance.terminalNote: The terminal keeps its dark ground in every theme. A shell paints its own ANSI colours for a dark background; on a white one they stop being readable.
about.privacySaid: What devpit keeps on this computer and what it ever sends.
about.licenceSaid: devpit is open source, under the Apache License 2.0.
about.noticesSaid: The notices of the work devpit includes.
archive.note: Conversations of {name} you archived from their menu. Restoring one puts it back in the lists.
pause.title: Pause
pause.said: Quiet for a meeting or a stretch of thought. Agents keep working.
pause.more: No notifications, the island neither opens nor sounds, and a terminal’s permission question goes straight to that terminal. Agents’ news is still heard and reminders still go off. Also in the status strip and the tray.
pause.resumeTitle: Resume: notifications, the island and its questions come back
onboarding.changeLater: You can change it later in Settings.
onboarding.projectSaid: A folder with a git repository in it. devpit reads it where it is and never moves it.
onboarding.browserCheck: . Check that it shows this code, then approve it there — this screen moves on by itself.
onboarding.signInTitle: Sign in, if you want to
onboarding.freeSaid: Free, and optional. It signs you in; sync between your computers is off until you turn it on, and carries only preferences and project settings, sealed so devpit.app cannot read them.
onboarding.stays: Your projects, conversations and files stay on this computer
